- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off or reversal bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to hold or overestimate; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 3–5 periods.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1) triggers model overreaction; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 2–4 periods to avoid “sentiment echo” bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
